the 4- and 6-parameter fractional-order models are able to accurately represent the averaged human body contact impedance from 40 MHz to 110 GHz with 4% and 2% error, respectively.
three different models with different numbers of parameters are able to represent the impedance of the human body against contact currents in the frequency range of 40 Hz-110 MHz.

developing fractional-order models of the impedance against contact currents of human bodies.
the development of fractional-order models of the human body impedance that can be used to represent this impedance over a wide frequency range.
developing compact fractional-order models of the human body impedance to be used in the design of safety standards for human exposure to contact currents.

the fractional-order models are more accurate than the already existing integer-order model.

the fractional-order models can be used to represent the human impedance with a smaller number of parameters than the integer-order model.
